extraInstructions: IMPORTANT: Do NOT use speechManager.speak() anywhere in the game. Only use audioManager.play() for sound effects. Valid sound effects: pickup, drop-correct, drop-wrong, tap, success, error, celebration, hint. The game must teach: (1) Simple graphs — a bar graph uses bars of different heights to show information. Tallest bar = most popular. Shortest bar = least popular. Graphs help us compare things easily. Example: favorite fruits graph — apple has 5 votes (tallest), banana has 3, mango has 4, orange has 2 (shortest). (2) Unit of repeat in patterns — a pattern has a unit that repeats. In Red, Blue, Red, Blue..., the unit is 'Red, Blue'. In Circle, Square, Triangle, Circle, Square, Triangle..., the unit is 'Circle, Square, Triangle'. Find the smallest repeating unit. (3) Extending patterns — once you find the unit of repeat, continue the pattern. Red, Yellow, Red, Yellow, Red, Yellow, Red... — the unit is 'Red, Yellow', so after Red comes Yellow, then Red. (4) Create patterns from daily life — patterns are everywhere: floor tiles (square, triangle, square, triangle), sari borders (flower, leaf, flower, leaf), necklaces (red bead, blue bead, red bead, blue bead), days of the week (Monday to Sunday, then repeats), months of the year. Children create their own patterns using colors, shapes, and objects. Misconceptions: 'any repeating thing is a pattern' (a pattern has a RULE that repeats — random repeating is not a pattern), 'the unit of repeat can be any part' (the unit of repeat is the SMALLEST part that repeats), 'tallest bar means least' (tallest bar means MOST, shortest bar means LEAST), 'patterns only exist in maths' (patterns are everywhere — in tiles, fabrics, nature, music, days of the week). Default width=720, height=560. Use named export (export function PatternsGame), NOT export default. Export interface PatternsGameProps with width?, height?, onComplete?: (score: number) => void.
